Compare latent class models

Source: R/lpa.R
enumerate_lca.Rd

enumerate_lca() fits latent class models with different numbers of classes to examine heterogeneity in categorical response patterns. It brings together evidence about fit, classification, and estimation stability to support selection of the number of classes. Each fitted candidate remains available for examination of its class-specific response probabilities and class proportions.

Usage

enumerate_lca(data, vars, n_classes = 1:4, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation.

vars

Names of the categorical indicator columns.

n_classes

Numbers of classes to compare, specified as positive integers.

...

Further arguments for multilca(), such as missing, n_starts, seed and min_probability, except id and n_group_classes. Every indicator is categorical unless named in ordinal or count. categorical is accepted but has no further effect; its names must be in vars.

Value

An object of class multilpa_enumeration, as enumerate_classes() returns: as.data.frame() gives one row per candidate, summary() the candidate minimizing each criterion, plot() the criteria against the number of classes, and get_candidate() one fitted candidate. The number of classes is reported in the n_profiles column of the enumeration table and selected through the n_profiles argument of get_candidate().

Details

This is the single-level interface to enumerate_classes() for categorical indicators. Every indicator is categorical unless named in ordinal or count, as in lca().

For observations nested in groups, use enumerate_classes() with the grouping column as id and the indicators as categorical.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument when id or n_group_classes is passed, or when model is passed (no indicator is continuous); latents_bad_categorical when categorical names a column not in vars.

See also

lca() to fit one model; enumerate_lpa() for continuous indicators.

Examples

models <- enumerate_lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends",
                                       "on_social_media", "sports"),
                        n_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#> Warning: The model is not identified: it has 11 free parameters, but its indicators' 8 response patterns leave only 7 free cell probabilities (-4 degrees of freedom). Its class sizes and response probabilities are not determined by the data; fit fewer classes or use more indicators.
summary(models)
#> Class enumeration: 3 candidates, 3 converged, 0 failed to fit
#> 2 distinct candidate(s) are minimal under some criterion.
#> No candidate is selected automatically. Choose one convention and keep it.
